Create the cover illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: On a windy spring day, Askeladden strides up the winding road towards the royal manor on its green rise, his brown cloak flapping, his bulging sack over his shoulder and a crooked goat horn in his hand. In the open door of the manor hall, the Princess stands waiting with her arms crossed and her chin up, one sharp eyebrow raised. White clouds race across the bright blue sky, and the young birch leaves shine yellow-green.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- Askeladden: A slim, lean young man of about eighteen with a clever, narrow face, sharp dark eyes that notice everything, straight black eyebrows, a thin straight nose and a lopsided, knowing smile. His black hair is shaggy and uncombed and falls over his ears and forehead. He wears a brown hooded wool cloak fastened with a wooden toggle over a knee-length ochre tunic with a woven belt, dark-grey trousers and soft brown leather shoes, and carries a patched brown sack.
- the Princess: A quick-witted princess of about eighteen, slim and upright, with a lively oval face, sharp, arched dark eyebrows, bright amber eyes, a small pointed nose and a mouth always ready with a clever reply. Her glossy chestnut hair is piled up in a high bun with a small silver crown pinned in front of it. She wears a long lilac wool gown with a fitted bodice, long sleeves and silver embroidery at the neckline, and small silver earrings.

Story world: Old rural Norway, long ago. The King's manor is a cluster of dark, tarred timber buildings with steep turf roofs on a green rise above ploughed fields where muck has just been spread, with a winding road and birch groves below. The Princess receives her suitors in the manor's hall, which has small-paned windows, walls painted with red and blue rosemaling flowers, a long carved oak table and the King's tall carved high seat. Askeladden's finds are a small ring of twisted green willow, a shard of a broken blue-and-white bowl, a dead black-and-white magpie, two crooked goat horns that look exactly alike, and an old, worn-out leather shoe sole with a hole right through it. He carries them in a patched brown sack.

This story's season, light and colours: A windy spring day: white clouds racing across a bright blue sky, fresh yellow-green birch leaves, young grass and dark, freshly manured fields, with cloaks, hair and grass all blowing in the wind. Inside the hall: clear, cool daylight through small windows on warm wood and red and blue rosemaling.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

characters.name: Askeladden
characters.description: The youngest brother, underestimated but quick-witted, who carries strange roadside items and turns the Princess’s jabs back on her.
characters.look: A slim, lean young man of about eighteen with a clever, narrow face, sharp dark eyes that notice everything, straight black eyebrows, a thin straight nose and a lopsided, knowing smile. His black hair is shaggy and uncombed and falls over his ears and forehead. He wears a brown hooded wool cloak fastened with a wooden toggle over a knee-length ochre tunic with a woven belt, dark-grey trousers and soft brown leather shoes, and carries a patched brown sack.

characters.name: The Princess
characters.description: A sharp-tongued, contrary royal who prides herself on always having the last word—until Askeladden leaves her speechless.
characters.look: A quick-witted princess of about eighteen, slim and upright, with a lively oval face, sharp, arched dark eyebrows, bright amber eyes, a small pointed nose and a mouth always ready with a clever reply. Her glossy chestnut hair is piled up in a high bun with a small silver crown pinned in front of it. She wears a long lilac wool gown with a fitted bodice, long sleeves and silver embroidery at the neckline, and small silver earrings.

characters.name: The King
characters.description: The ruler who promises his daughter and half the kingdom to anyone who can silence her.
characters.look: A tired, stooped, elderly king with a long, gentle, wrinkled face, sleepy grey eyes with heavy bags under them, bushy grey eyebrows and a huge, drooping grey moustache that hangs down past his chin, but no beard. He wears a long mustard-yellow robe with a brown fur collar, a simple gold crown that always sits askew, and soft brown slippers.

illustrations.anchor: And then the Princess was tongue-tied.
illustrations.caption: And then the Princess was tongue-tied.
illustrations.alt: The Princess stands open-mouthed in the hall, unable to get a word out. Askeladden holds up a worn-out shoe sole, and the King leans forward on his throne.

In his carved high seat, the King leans forward, gripping the armrests in astonishment.
